cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z (1999) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414 (deposit, nesting structure); Meyers BC, Tingey SV, Morgante M (2001) Genome Res 11(10):1660-1676, Table 1 (independent Ty1-copia classification of the Ji family)
cases.why_safe: Ji is grouped as a Ty1-copia-like family by RT-based phylogenetic clustering in SanMiguel et al. 1996/1998 and independently tabulated as copia in Meyers et al. 2001 Table 1 -- a classification made without reference to this specific deposit or to TEagle. In THIS deposit, the ji_334B07-3 mobile_element feature is annotated as three disjoint plus-strand segments (66750-68627 / 77590-81762 / 83018-86042) with a ~9-kb opie (Copia) element nested in the first gap on the complement strand and a ji solo LTR filling the second gap -- i.e. the coding span is fragmented and interleaved with an opposite-strand insertion in this exact record, independent of whether TEagle's IN/RT domain calls happen to fall across the break.

cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z (1999) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414 (deposit, nesting structure); Meyers BC, Tingey SV, Morgante M (2001) Genome Res 11(10):1660-1676, Table 1 (independent Ty1-copia classification of the Victim family)
cases.why_safe: Victim is independently classified as Ty1-copia in Meyers et al. 2001 Table 1, a phylogeny-based family assignment made without reference to this deposit or to TEagle. In this record the element is annotated as four minus-strand segments spanning ~35 kb (64409-65235 / 66407-66749 / 86043-90234 / 99573-99651), interleaved with a ji solo LTR and the nested ji/opie complex described above -- among the most fragmented arrangements in the record, so any reading of IN vs RT order from this deposit alone would require reconstructing across three separate opposite-orientation insertions.

cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z (1999) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414 (deposit, nesting structure); Meyers BC, Tingey SV, Morgante M (2001) Genome Res 11(10):1660-1676, Table 1 (independent Ty3-gypsy classification of the Milt family)
cases.why_safe: Milt is independently tabulated as Ty3-gypsy in Meyers et al. 2001 Table 1, a classification derived from RT phylogeny, not from this deposit or from TEagle. Here milt_334B07-1 is annotated as two plus-strand segments (23707-24145 and 33140-37493) with a ~9-kb opie (Copia) element nested between them on the complement strand. Confidence is lower than the other two cases because the first segment is short (439 bp) and I could not confirm from the flatfile alone that the IN and RT coding sub-regions of milt actually straddle the break rather than both lying within the larger 33140-37493 segment -- this would need a protein-level domain map of milt to confirm, which the GenBank record does not provide.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Text states directly: 'the sequence similarity index of the LTRs for the seven transposons in the cluster are as follows: Zeon1, 100%...' Zeon1 copy at the top of the 94-kb nested retrotransposon cluster in the Bz-McC bz1-locus sequence (AF391808). Family originally characterized by Meyers, Tingey & Morgante (Cinful-Zeon, Ty3/gypsy). Youngest member of this locus's spread. Exact bp coordinates within AF391808 not resolved from the text (nesting order only, Fig. 1 of the source paper).

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly in text: 'Fourf, 98.2%' LTR-LTR identity, an intact element inserted into the RIRE1-like element in the same 94-kb nest (Fig. 1). Fourf family originally described by SanMiguel et al. 1996 Science as a Ty1/copia element near maize Adh1.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'RIRE1, 97.1%' LTR-LTR identity for the element interrupted by Fourf in the nest. RIRE1 was first characterized as a copia-like element in wild rice (Noma et al. 1997); its presence here reflects a conserved ancient Ty1/copia lineage cross-referenced by name in the maize literature -- family-level call carries slightly more uncertainty than the identity number itself.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'Prem1, 94.6%' LTR-LTR identity, an internally deleted Prem1 element noted near the stk1 gene in the same locus. PREM-1 was originally described by Turcich et al. 1996 as a pollen-transcribed maize retroelement; exact Ty1/copia vs Ty3/gypsy call for PREM-1 specifically (as opposed to its relative PREM-2) was not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'Prem2b, 91.6%' LTR-LTR identity. This is the distal Prem2 copy in the nest, itself interrupted by a CACTA-family DNA transposon. PREM-2 was characterized as a copia-type retroelement by Turcich et al. 1996. Solidly in the 85-97% intermediate band.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'Opie2, 91.2%' LTR-LTR identity for a 'full-size but probably nonfunctional' Opie2 element inserted into the base Prem2-a. Opie is a well-established maize Ty1/copia family (SanMiguel et al. 1996).

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'Huck2, 85.8%' LTR-LTR identity for an incomplete Huck2 element in the nest. Huck is a well-established maize Ty3/gypsy family (SanMiguel et al. 1996). Sits right at the top edge of the 72-84% floor band.

cases.citation: Fu H, Zheng Z & Dooner HK 2002 PNAS 99:1082
cases.why_safe: Stated directly: 'Prem2a, 63.8%' LTR-LTR identity -- the most diverged element in the cluster, described by the authors as 'a highly fragmented Prem2 element at its base' of the 81-kb nest. This is the single clearly-degraded (<72%) case recovered in this search; confidence is tempered because 'highly fragmented' may mean the aligned LTR remnants are partial rather than full-length termini.

cases.citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK & Lenz J 2001 Current Biology 11:1531
cases.why_safe: Turner et al. sequenced both LTRs of this human-specific, insertionally polymorphic provirus and found 'no sequence differences between the 5' and 3' LTR' -- i.e., 100% LTR-LTR identity -- giving an estimated insertion time of 100,000-200,000 years. HML-2/LTR5Hs family membership is established by prior phylogenetic classification (Mayer/Coffin lineage work) independent of any TE-annotation tool. Youngest anchor of the >=98% bucket, cross-kingdom counterpart to the fly data.

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Subramanian et al. report an estimated age of 1.61-2.91 My for this human-specific, polymorphic HML-2 locus, calculated from LTR-LTR substitution frequency divided by their stated clock (0.24%/My upper bound, 0.45%/My lower bound). Back-solving that formula gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of roughly 99.3% (substitution ~0.7%) -- a value I derived from their stated rate and age range, not a percentage printed directly in the paper, hence medium rather than high confidence on the exact number (the accession and HML-2 family call are high confidence).

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Human-specific, polymorphic HML-2 locus with reported age 4.87-8.82 My. Using the paper's own stated clock (substitution% = age x 0.24 to 0.45), the implied LTR-LTR identity is ~97.8-98% -- derived by me from their stated formula, not a printed percentage. Coordinates and chromosome given directly in the paper (GRCh37/hg19); accession is the standard GRCh37.p13 chr8 RefSeq record.

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Human-specific HML-2 locus, reported age 6.32-11.44 My. Applying the paper's stated substitution-rate formula gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of ~97.2% (derived, not printed directly). Falls at the top of the 85-97% intermediate band.

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Orangutan-shared HML-2 locus, reported age 12.13-21.96 My. Applying the paper's stated clock gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of ~94.6% (derived from stated age range and rate, not a printed percentage). Solid mid-intermediate example from a non-rodent, non-plant, non-insect lineage.

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Rhesus-macaque-shared HML-2 locus, reported age 14.17-25.65 My, the second-oldest dated locus in the catalogue. Implied LTR-LTR identity ~93.7% via the paper's stated clock (derived, not printed directly).

cases.citation: Subramanian RP, Wildschutte JH, Russo C & Coffin JM 2011 Retrovirology 8:90
cases.why_safe: Oldest dated locus in the Subramanian catalogue (23.46-42.48 My, oldest common ancestor unknown). Applying the paper's own substitution-rate formula gives an implied LTR-LTR identity of only ~89.6% even at this maximal age -- illustrating why the very slow primate ERV clock (0.24-0.45%/My) cannot by itself supply examples at or below the 72-84% floor; identity is derived, not printed directly, hence medium confidence.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (myosin heavy chain, unc-54), single-copy genomic clone with 8 introns
cases.coords: 909-8178 (join across 9 exons / 8 introns per the CDS join in the GenBank record; introns 48-561 bp)
cases.citation: Karn J, Brenner S, Barnett L (1983) Protein structural domains in the Caenorhabditis elegans unc-54 myosin heavy chain gene are not separated by introns. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 80(14):4253-4257
cases.why_safe: Single-copy sarcomeric myosin gene; the 9-kb genomic clone contains only the unc-54 CDS and its introns, all of which are far too short (48-561 bp) to harbor a full DNA-transposon or retroelement insertion. No TE is reported at this locus in the primary structural characterization.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (vegetative actin, ACT2), single-copy genomic clone with 2 introns
cases.coords: 597-2849 (mRNA span; CDS exons 1217-1670, 1749-2362, 2449-2514 per GenBank feature table)
cases.citation: An YQ, McDowell JM, Huang S, McKinney EC, Chambliss S, Meagher RB (1996) Strong, constitutive expression of the Arabidopsis ACT2/ACT8 actin subclass in vegetative tissues. Plant J 10(1):107-121
cases.why_safe: Single-copy vegetative actin gene deposited as a discrete 3172-bp genomic clone. Both introns lie entirely within this well-characterized coding region and no TE insertion is reported in the reference clone.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (actin, ACT1), single-copy essential gene with one intron
cases.citation: NCBI Gene ID 850504 (ACT1/YFL039C), cross-referenced to Saccharomyces Genome Database locus S000001855, chromosome VI reference sequence NC_001138.5
cases.why_safe: ACT1 is single-copy and essential; its one intron is only ~308 bp, far too short to contain a Ty retrotransposon (~5.9 kb) or even a full solo LTR. Ty elements in S. cerevisiae preferentially target Pol III-transcribed (tRNA-gene-flanking) regions, not ACT1.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host protein-coding gene (beta-globin, HBB), single-copy gene with 2 introns
cases.coords: 62137-63742 (HBB gene per GenBank feature table; introns at 62279-62408 and 62632-63481)
cases.citation: Lawn RM, Efstratiadis A, O'Connell C, Maniatis T (1980) The nucleotide sequence of the human beta-globin gene. Cell 21(3):647-651
cases.why_safe: HBB is the archetypal single-copy globin gene; coordinates are restricted to the gene body itself (both short introns), which has been sequenced and studied for over 40 years with no TE insertion reported within it, unlike the Alu-containing intergenic/LCR regions elsewhere in this 73-kb clone.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - centromeric alpha-satellite tandem repeat (171-bp AT-rich consensus monomer); satellite DNA, not a mobile element
cases.citation: Vissel B, Choo KH (1987) Human alpha satellite DNA--consensus sequence and conserved regions. Nucleic Acids Res 15(16):6751-6752
cases.why_safe: Alpha satellite is a tandemly repeated, non-autonomous, non-mobile DNA family confined to centromeric regions. It has no ORF and no similarity to transposase/RT domains, so it is a risk mainly for repeat-content-based (not domain-based) callers.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - simple/low-complexity CGG trinucleotide microsatellite in the FMR1 5' UTR
cases.coords: 2720-2767 (CGG repeat_region as annotated in the GenBank record)
cases.citation: Fu YH, Kuhl DP, Pizzuti A, et al. (1991) Variation of the CGG repeat at the fragile X site results in genetic instability: resolution of the Sherman paradox. Cell 67(6):1047-1058
cases.why_safe: Pure trinucleotide microsatellite with no coding capacity. Its GC-richness and copy-number polymorphism can trigger low-complexity/simple-repeat masking, but it has no similarity to any TE domain or terminal-repeat structure.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT/hEST2), single-copy nuclear gene, mRNA/complete cds
cases.citation: Meyerson M, Counter CM, Eaton EN, et al. (1997) hEST2, the putative human telomerase catalytic subunit gene, is up-regulated in tumor cells and during immortalization. Cell 90(4):785-795
cases.why_safe: TERT carries a bona fide reverse-transcriptase fold and is a top false-positive risk for RT-domain-based TE detectors; it is single-copy, nuclear-encoded, essential for telomere maintenance, and its RT activity was directly assayed biochemically on the telomerase RNA template, independent of any TE annotation.

cases.expected_class: reverse-transcriptase domain of a self-splicing group II intron (Ll.LtrB, protein LtrA) - falls outside the Wicker eukaryotic TE classification scheme rather than being a TE proper
cases.citation: Mills DA, McKay LL, Dunny GM (1996) Splicing of a group II intron involved in the conjugative transfer of pRS01 in lactococci. J Bacteriol 178(12):3531-3538
cases.why_safe: LtrA has an authentic RT domain, evolutionarily ancestral to non-LTR retrotransposon and telomerase RTs, and is a frequent close bacterial hit for RT-domain searches. Ll.LtrB is nonetheless a catalytic-RNA self-splicing intron with an intron-encoded protein (retrohoming mechanism) rather than a Wicker-scheme transposable element; its single-copy context interrupting the conjugative relaxase gene ltrB was established experimentally, independent of any TE caller. Labeled with a softened class string rather than a flat 'not a TE' because group II introns are themselves mobile genetic elements under some classification schemes.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host AP endonuclease (APEX1/APE1/HAP1), single-copy base-excision-repair enzyme
cases.citation: Robson CN, Hickson ID (1991) Isolation of cDNA clones encoding a human apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease that corrects DNA repair and mutagenesis defects in E. coli xth (exonuclease III) mutants. Nucleic Acids Res 19(20):5519-5523
cases.why_safe: APE1 belongs to the Exo_endo_phos (DNase I-like) nuclease superfamily that also contains the endonuclease domain of LINE-1 ORF2p, so domain-based TE callers keyed on this fold risk flagging APE1. It is single-copy, essential, nuclear-encoded, carries no RT or transposase domain, and its AP-endonuclease activity was defined biochemically independent of any TE annotation.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host chromosomal tyrosine recombinase (XerC), single-copy site-specific recombinase for chromosome-dimer resolution
cases.citation: Colloms SD, Sykora P, Szatmari G, Sherratt DJ (1990) Recombination at ColE1 cer requires the Escherichia coli xerC gene product, a member of the lambda integrase family of site-specific recombinases. J Bacteriol 172(12):6973-6980
cases.why_safe: XerC is a catalytic-tyrosine site-specific recombinase of the lambda-integrase family. This tyrosine-recombinase fold, rather than the DDE-transposase fold used by most DNA transposons, is what Crypton DNA transposons and DIRS-like retroelements use for integration, making it a genuine confusion axis for domain panels. XerC's role in dif-site recombination for chromosome dimer resolution was established biochemically and genetically, independent of any TE database.

cases.expected_class: not a TE - host spliceosomal protein (PRP8/YHR165C) whose core domain is a degenerate, catalytically repurposed reverse transcriptase/maturase/endonuclease/RNase-H-like fold retained from an ancestral retroelement
cases.citation: Dlakic M, Mushegian A (2011) Prp8, the pivotal protein of the spliceosomal catalytic center, evolved from a retroelement-encoded reverse transcriptase. RNA 17(5):799-808
cases.why_safe: PRP8's central conserved domain is structurally homologous to group-II-intron-maturase/retroelement RT-fingers-palm, thumb/X, and endonuclease-like subdomains - almost the full TE RT+EN domain architecture - yet it is single-copy, essential, and functions as the catalytic scaffold of the spliceosome, not as a mobile element; its RT-like fold is catalytically dead/repurposed, established by structural and phylogenetic analysis independent of any TE caller.

cases.citation: Emori Y, Shiba T, Kanaya S, Inouye S, Yuki S, Saigo K. 1985. Nature 315:773-776
cases.why_safe: Original full-length sequencing of the Drosophila copia element (the type element of the Copia/Ty1 superfamily); complete 5183 bp record independently verified on GenBank (not TEagle's bundled M11240 example).

cases.citation: Boeke JD, Eichinger D, Castrillon D, Fink GR. 1988. Mol Cell Biol 8(4):1432-1442
cases.why_safe: Ty1-H3, a genomic Ty1 copy; Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ty1 is the ICTV type species of Pseudoviridae (Ty1/copia lineage), so superfamily assignment is independent of any de novo classifier.

cases.citation: Janetzky B, Lehle L. 1992. J Biol Chem 267(28):19798-19805
cases.why_safe: Ty4, flanked by tau solo-LTR elements; Ty4 groups with the Ty1/copia (Pseudoviridae) lineage of S. cerevisiae Ty elements. Note: TY4A gag is annotated as a pseudogene, TY4B protease-integrase-RT/RNase H (pol) is complete cds -- useful mainly for pol-domain content, not full gag-pol boundary testing.

cases.citation: Grandbastien MA, Spielmann A, Caboche M. 1989. Nature 337:376-380
cases.why_safe: Tnt1-94, the first fully sequenced active plant retrotransposon, described as a copia-like LTR retroelement with gag-pol organization typical of Ty1/copia elements.

cases.citation: Manninen I, Schulman AH. 1993. Plant Mol Biol 22(5):829-846
cases.why_safe: BARE-1, described as a copia-like retroelement; paper states LTRs of 1829 bp with 6 bp inverted terminal repeats flanking an internal domain homologous to gag, pro, int and rt of copia-like retrotransposons.

cases.citation: Laten HM, Majumdar A, Gaucher EA. 1998. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 95(12):6897-6902
cases.why_safe: SIRE1-1, explicitly described as a copia/Ty1-like retroelement with gag-pro-int-rt-rh domain order plus an unusual retroviral env-like ORF; superfamily assignment made independently by domain-order phylogeny.

cases.citation: SanMiguel P, Tikhonov A, Jin YK, et al. 1996. Science 274(5288):765-768
cases.why_safe: Opie-2, one of the maize Adh1-region retrotransposon families characterized in the classic nested-retrotransposon paper; record covers 5' LTR, PBS, gag and complete pol cds of the Opie (Ty1/copia) family.

cases.citation: Avedisov SN, Cherkasova VA, Il'in YV. 1990. Genetika 26(11):1905-1914
cases.why_safe: mdg1, a classic Drosophila copia-like element (grouped with copia, 1731, 297, mdg1 as the canonical Ty1/copia-like Drosophila families); 7480 bp record independently deposited, distinct from any excluded development accession.

cases.citation: Fourcade-Peronnet F, d'Auriol L, Becker J, Galibert F, Best-Belpomme M. 1988. Nucleic Acids Res 16(13):6113-6125
cases.why_safe: Retrotransposon 1731, full-length 4648 bp copy flanked by 336 bp LTRs (paper-stated), part of the Ty1/copia-like Drosophila element group.

cases.citation: Camirand A, Brisson N. 1990. Nucleic Acids Res 18(16):4929
cases.why_safe: Tst1, the first completely sequenced potato transposable element, explicitly described as copia-like; paper states 5' and 3' LTRs of 285 and 283 bp respectively flanking a 5060 bp element.

cases.citation: Lucas H, Moore G, Murphy G, Flavell RB. 1992. Mol Biol Evol 9(4):716-728
cases.why_safe: WIS2-1A, a copia-like wheat retrotransposon; this specific record (1755 bp) is a cloned LTR-containing fragment, not the full internal domain -- useful for LTR/inverted-repeat structure (the paper's focus) but not for full-length boundary testing.

cases.citation: Voytas DF, Ausubel FM. 1988. Nature 336:242-244
cases.why_safe: Ta1-3, a member of the Ta1 copia-like transposable element family of A. thaliana; ORF shows clear similarity to the Drosophila copia polyprotein, cited as the basis for copia-like classification.

cases.citation: Hu W, Das OP, Messing J. 1995. Mol Gen Genet 248(4):471-480
cases.why_safe: Zeon-1, 7313 bp record length matches the paper-stated element size exactly; paper describes two LTRs, PBS, PPT and a gag-related ORF diagnostic of a copia-like (Ty1) element.

cases.citation: Ohbayashi F, Shimada T, Sugasaki T, Kawai S, Mita K, Oshiki T, Abe H. 1998. Genes Genet Syst 73(6):345-352
cases.why_safe: Yokozuna, described as the first Ty1/copia LTR retrotransposon characterized in the silkworm genome (W chromosome); complete cds record, 4738 bp.

cases.citation: Rohr CJ, Ranson H, Wang X, Besansky NJ. 2002. Mol Biol Evol 19(2):149-162
cases.why_safe: mtanga, a Y-chromosome-linked Ty1/copia retrotransposon shown to be actively transcribed in A. gambiae; complete-sequence record, 4284 bp, independent of any TEagle output.

cases.citation: Flavell AJ, Jackson V, Iqbal MP, Riach I, Waddell S. 1995. Mol Gen Genet 246(1):65-71
cases.why_safe: Tpa1, an amphibian Ty1-copia group RT-domain sequence placed within the Ty1/copia clade by phylogenetic analysis in the primary paper. Caveat: this is a short (~225 bp) degenerate-primer PCR fragment of the RT catalytic core, not a full-length element -- useful only for taxonomic-spread superfamily calls, not for LTR-boundary or full-domain-content testing. Included because full-length vertebrate Copia elements are essentially unavailable as discrete GenBank records.

cases.coords: complement(3902..12543) within FJ173819 [3' LTR complement(3902..5667); 5' LTR complement(10775..12543)]
cases.citation: Distelfeld A, Tranquilli G, Li C, Yan L, Dubcovsky J. 2009. Plant Physiol 149(1):245-257
cases.why_safe: The record's own feature-table annotation labels this mobile element a Copia-type retrotransposon (family Angela, well established in wheat literature) with explicit 5'/3' LTR coordinates (~1.7 kb each) flanked by target-site duplications; the cited paper's own focus is the adjacent VRN2 (ZCCT1-B1) gene, not Angela -- superfamily call rests on the GenBank annotation itself, not on that paper's argument.

cases.citation: Verries C, Bes M, This P, Tesniere C. 2000. Genome 43(2):366-376
cases.why_safe: VINE-1, a Ty1/copia-like grapevine retrotransposon (grouped with Tvv1 as Copia, versus the Ty3/gypsy-like Gret1, in the grapevine TE literature); this GenBank record's own gag-pol complete cds spans 5321 bp, a fuller-length family member than the ~2392 bp truncated copy inserted in the Adhr gene that the cited paper's abstract centers on -- same family, same citation, different copy length.

cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z. 1999. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414
cases.why_safe: A second, non-truncated Opie-family (Ty1/copia) copy explicitly annotated with element coordinates in the finished maize adh1 region sequence; family assignment (Opie/Ty1-copia) independently established in SanMiguel et al. 1996 Science and reaffirmed in this paper's annotation.

cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z. 1999. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414
cases.why_safe: A non-truncated Ji-family copy (the Ji/Opie lineage is Ty1/copia) annotated with explicit element coordinates in the finished maize adh1 region; distinct locus from the opie_334B07-3 entry above, same BAC/region.

cases.citation: Inouye S, Yuki S, Saigo K. 1986. Eur J Biochem 154(2):417-425
cases.why_safe: Complete 6995 bp sequence of element 297, one of the canonical gypsy-clade Drosophila families (gypsy, 297, 17.6, ZAM); three ORFs comparable to retroviral gag, pol and env.

cases.citation: Pelissier T, Tutois S, Deragon JM, Tourmente S, Genestier S, Picard G. 1995. Plant Mol Biol 29(3):441-452
cases.why_safe: Athila, explicitly assigned to the gypsy retrotransposon class; paper states ~10.5 kb elements flanked by ~1.5 kb LTRs with retroviral 5'TG...CA3' termini, many with an env-containing ORF3.

cases.citation: Pantazidis A, Labrador M, Fontdevila A. 1999. Mol Biol Evol 16(7):909-921
cases.why_safe: Osvaldo, described as displaying all structural features of a functional retrovirus, distantly related to gypsy; paper states 9045 bp total length with 1196 bp LTRs; record length (9085 bp) matches closely.

cases.citation: Britten RJ. 1995. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 92:599-601
cases.why_safe: Cer1, an 8865 bp complete gag-pol-env cds record explicitly identified as a gypsy/Ty3 retrotransposon/retrovirus of C. elegans.

cases.citation: Farman ML, Tosa Y, Nitta N, Leong SA. 1996. Mol Gen Genet 251(6):665-674
cases.why_safe: MAGGY, described as closely related to the gypsy class based on gag-pol-env-like ORF organization. Caveat: this record's gag gene is partial (5' truncated, '<' in feature table); only the pol (RT) region is complete cds -- usable for pol-domain content, not full gag boundary testing.

cases.citation: Leblanc P, Desset S, Dastugue B, Vaury C. 1997. EMBO J 16(24):7521-7531
cases.why_safe: ZAM, shown experimentally to have all structural (gag-pol-env) and functional features of a retrovirus and grouped with the canonical gypsy clade (gypsy, 297, 17.6, ZAM); complete 8435 bp gag/pol/env record.

cases.citation: Desset S, Conte C, Dimitri P, Calco V, Dastugue B, Vaury C. 1999. Mol Biol Evol 16(1):54-66
cases.why_safe: Idefix, characterized alongside ZAM as a mobilized gypsy-clade retroelement regulated by the flamenco locus. Record is explicitly labeled 'partial' (gag/pol/env genes, partial), 7411 bp -- useful for domain content but not guaranteed full-length boundaries.

cases.citation: Molto MD, Paricio N, Lopez-Preciado MA, Semeshin VF, Martinez-Sebastian MJ. 1996. J Mol Evol 42:369-375
cases.why_safe: Tirant, described as gag-pol-env organized and strongly similar to ZAM, part of the gypsy-clade tirant/zam/idefix/17.6/297 group; record is 5184 bp, shorter than the ~8527 bp full-length element reported in later work, so likely represents a partial/defective genomic copy rather than the complete consensus.

cases.citation: Sanz-Alferez S, SanMiguel P, Jin YK, Springer PS, Bennetzen JL. 2003. Genome 46(5):745-752
cases.why_safe: Cinful-1, an 8581 bp complete-sequence record, explicitly classified as Ty3-gypsy type. Caveat: the paper reports Cinful-1/2 lack gag homology (a defective element for gag content), so this record is best used for pol/LTR structure rather than full gag-pol-env domain testing.

cases.citation: SanMiguel P, Bennetzen JL. 1998. Ann Bot 82(Suppl A):37-44
cases.why_safe: Tekay, explicitly titled in GenBank as a 'gypsy/Ty3-type retrotransposon,' complete 12118 bp sequence.

cases.citation: Avramova Z, Tikhonov A, SanMiguel P, Jin YK, Liu C, Woo SS, Wing RA, Bennetzen JL. 1996. Plant J 10(6):1163-1168
cases.why_safe: Reina, explicitly deposited as a 'Gypsy-like retrotransposon'; 5412 bp record from the paper that first named and localized this low-copy maize element.

cases.citation: Butler M, Goodwin T, Poulter R. 2001. Mol Biol Evol 18(3):443-447
cases.why_safe: Gmr1, a full-length (5269 bp) vertebrate LTR retrotransposon placed in the Ty3/gypsy group by sequence-similarity phylogeny, with LTRs stated to be 98% identical. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Gmr1 has an unusual pol domain order (protease-integrase-RT/RNase H) matching the Ty1/copia arrangement rather than the canonical Ty3/gypsy protease-RT/RNase H-integrase order -- this is a documented exception explicitly discussed by the authors, not a labeling error, and should be treated as a deliberately atypical stress-test case rather than a canonical Gypsy exemplar if domain order is part of the classifier's decision logic.

cases.citation: Rocheta M, Cordeiro J, Marum L, Farinha N, Amaral P, Sobral R, Miguel C. 2012. BMC Res Notes 5:432
cases.why_safe: Corky, explicitly deposited as a gypsy-like retrotransposon, complete 5924 bp sequence, homologous to other characterized Pinaceae gypsy elements (IFG7, PpRT1).

cases.citation: McHale MT, Roberts IN, Noble SA, Beaumont C, Whitehead MP, Seth D, Oliver RP. 1992. Mol Gen Genet 233(3):337-347
cases.why_safe: CfT-1, complete 7397 bp sequence; paper states LTRs of 427 bp and a pol ORF with domain order protease-RT-RNaseH-integrase, closely related to the gypsy class of LTR retrotransposons. Current species name is Fulvia fulva (synonym of Cladosporium fulvum).

cases.citation: Dobinson KF, Harris RE, Hamer JE. 1993. Mol Plant Microbe Interact 6:114-126
cases.why_safe: Grasshopper (grh), complete gag/pol cds (5233 bp); paper states 198 bp LTRs and a pol ORF (RT-RNaseH-integrase order) related to the gypsy family.

cases.citation: Kobayashi S, Goto-Yamamoto N, Hirochika H. 2004. Science 304(5673):982
cases.why_safe: Gret1, explicitly deposited/titled as a 'gypsy-type retrotransposon'; its insertion into the VvMybA1 promoter was experimentally linked to loss of grape skin pigmentation, an independent functional confirmation of the element's identity and locus.

cases.citation: Anaya N, Roncero MI. 1995. Mol Gen Genet 249(6):637-647
cases.why_safe: Skippy, complete gag/pol cds (8457 bp); paper states 429 bp LTRs and a pol domain order (protease-RT-RNaseH-integrase) closely related to the gypsy family.

cases.citation: Kossack DS, Kinlaw CS. 1999. Plant Mol Biol 39(3):417-426
cases.why_safe: IFG7, deposited as 'gypsy-like retroposon...complete genome' (5937 bp); paper title states it 'has an extensive history in pines' and confirms gypsy-like sequence features.

cases.citation: Rocheta M, Cordeiro J, Oliveira M, Miguel C. 2007. Planta 225(3):551-562
cases.why_safe: PpRT1, the paper's title states it is 'the first complete gypsy-like retrotransposon isolated in Pinus pinaster'; complete-sequence record, 5966 bp, matching the paper's stated length.

cases.citation: Salina EA, Sergeeva EM, Adonina IG, Shcherban AB, Belcram H, Huneau C, Chalhoub B. 2011. BMC Plant Biol 11:99
cases.why_safe: One of three Fatima (Ty3-gypsy) elements explicitly annotated with coordinates in this BAC sequence; both flanking LTRs are 473 bp (5' 102728-103200, 3' 112206-112678), an unusually clean matched-LTR pair useful for panel 5.2 boundary comparison. Flanked by an ACATC target-site duplication per the annotation.

cases.citation: Tikhonov AP, SanMiguel PJ, Nakajima Y, Gorenstein NM, Bennetzen JL, Avramova Z. 1999. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 96(13):7409-7414
cases.why_safe: A non-truncated Huck-family (Ty3/gypsy) copy with explicit element coordinates annotated in the finished maize adh1 region; Huck superfamily assignment independently established in the maize LTR-retrotransposon literature (SanMiguel/Bennetzen lineage of papers).

cases.citation: Kimberland ML, Divoky V, Prchal J, Schwahn U, Berger W, Kazazian HH Jr. 1999. Hum Mol Genet 8(8):1557-1560
cases.why_safe: L1RP, a full-length, retrotransposition-competent ('hot') human L1 in intron 1 of the RP2 gene. GenBank record (6019 bp) annotates intact ORF1 (338 codons) and ORF2 (1275 codons; nt 1987-5814). L1 elements canonically terminate in a poly-A tail required for target-primed reverse transcription (Feng et al. 1996 Cell 87:905-916); this is clade-level structural knowledge, not a base-by-base re-verification of this specific record's terminal poly-A tract in this session.

cases.citation: Naas TP, DeBerardinis RJ, Moran JV, Ostertag EM, Kingsmore SF, Seldin MF, Hayashizaki Y, Martin SL, Kazazian HH Jr. 1998. EMBO J 17(2):590-597
cases.why_safe: L1spa (TF subfamily), a full-length, retrotransposition-competent mouse L1 that inserted de novo into the Glrb gene causing the spastic mouse phenotype (Kingsmore et al. 1994 Nat Genet 7:136-141). GenBank record (9278 bp) annotates ORF1 (nt 3142-4257) and ORF2 (nt 4298-8143). Naas et al. 1998 explicitly state a 667 bp 3' UTR 'terminating in a stretch of adenines' — poly-A tail directly confirmed in the primary paper, not inferred.

cases.citation: Fawcett DH, Lister CK, Kellett E, Finnegan DJ. 1986. Cell 47(6):1007-1015
cases.why_safe: Full-length I-factor clone (6231 bp) with annotated ORF1 (nt 286-1566) and ORF2 (nt 1635-5294). Importantly, I elements do NOT terminate in a poly-A tail: primary literature (Chambeyron et al. 2002 Nucleic Acids Res 30:3387-3395) established that I-clade elements end instead in 3-8 tandem TAA/UAA repeats. Full-length, non-poly-A-tailed structural contrast case.

cases.citation: Priimagi AF, Mizrokhi LJ, Ilyin YV. 1988. Gene 70(2):253-262
cases.why_safe: Near full-length Jockey clone 'J-1' (5154 bp; ORF1 <414-2165, 5' end of ORF1 slightly beyond the clone's UTR margin; ORF2 2162-4912). Priimagi et al. 1988 explicitly state a complete jockey copy 'is terminated with an oligodeoxynucleotide (dA) sequence' -- i.e. a poly(dA)/poly-A-like 3' tail, consistent with the terminal A-rich stretch of this record. Positive control for a poly-A-tailed LINE outside the L1/L1-related clades.

cases.citation: Fujimoto H, et al. 2004. Nucleic Acids Res 32(4):1555-1565; clade originally described by Burke WD, Müller F, Eickbush TH. 1987. Mol Cell Biol 7(6):2221-2230
cases.why_safe: R2Bm element (~4.2 kb) inserted into the 28S rRNA gene; single ORF (nt 658-4002) fusing reverse transcriptase and restriction-enzyme-like endonuclease domains -- the diagnostic R2-clade architecture (no separate ORF1/gag-like domain). R2 elements are established in the primary literature (Burke et al. 1987; Eickbush 2002 in Mobile DNA II) to lack a poly-A tail, instead ending in a structured, self-priming 3' UTR; the terminal ~80 nt of this record are GC-rich/structured rather than a homopolymeric A-tract, consistent with that.

cases.citation: Jakubczak JL, Xiong Y, Eickbush TH. 1990. J Mol Biol 212(1):37-52
cases.why_safe: Full-length-scale R1Dm clone (5356 bp) with two ORFs: ORF I (nt 319-1734, protease-like) and ORF II (nt 1728-4793, reverse transcriptase/integrase) -- the R1(LOA)-clade domain architecture, sister clade to R2. Superfamily left blank because R1-clade Wicker-superfamily naming is not fully standardized; clade identity (R1) is unambiguous. Like R2, R1 elements lack a canonical poly-A tail; the 3' terminus here is AT-rich rather than a homopolymeric A stretch.

cases.citation: Burke WD, Müller F, Eickbush TH. 1995. Nucleic Acids Res 23(22):4628-4634
cases.why_safe: Full-length R4 element (4686 bp) inserted into the 26S (large-subunit) rRNA gene. R4 is an ancient non-LTR clade encoding only a single ORF (restriction-enzyme-like endonuclease domain, no separate ORF1/gag-like domain) -- structurally distinct from L1/I/Jockey/R1/R2. Superfamily left blank (R4 clade, not a standard Wicker superfamily label) but the clade assignment itself is not in doubt. Useful single-ORF, non-poly-A contrast case.

cases.citation: Youngman S, van Luenen HGAM, Plasterk RHA. 1996. FEBS Lett 380(1-2):1-7
cases.why_safe: Complete RTE-1 element (3291 bp) with a single ORF (~625 aa, RT-similar) -- the RTE-clade single-ORF architecture (RTE established as a distinct, widely distributed clade by Malik & Eickbush 1998 Mol Biol Evol 15:1123-1134). Full-length, structurally simple non-LTR retrotransposon distinct from all L1/I/Jockey/R1/R2/R4 cases above.

cases.citation: Zatsepina OG, Velikodvorskaia VV, Molodtsov VB, Garbuz D, Lerman DN, Bettencourt BR, Feder ME, Evgen'ev MB. 2001. J Exp Biol 204(Pt 11):1869-1881
cases.why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case. GenBank explicitly annotates a 'truncated Jockey element transposon' at nt 360-1806 (1446 bp) adjacent to the Hsp70Ba gene -- roughly 29% of the ~5020 bp full-length Jockey (compare M22874 above), i.e. missing the 5' end and retaining only part of the element. Direct positive example of the common truncated genomic state for this clade; poly-A/3' status not separately assessed since the truncation removed the diagnostic 5' region, not the 3' end.

cases.citation: Woods-Samuels P, Wong C, Mathias SL, Scott AF, Kazazian HH Jr, Antonarakis SE. 1989. Genomics 4(3):290-296
cases.why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case (clone JH27L1HS, 3785 bp). Woods-Samuels et al. 1989 characterize this as a nondeleterious L1 insertion in an intron of the human factor VIII gene retaining an ORF spanning most of the clone (nt 1-3580), corresponding to the 3' portion of L1 ORF2 -- i.e. 5' end missing, 3' portion retained. Truncation and clade identity are established directly in the primary paper; the terminal poly-A tract specifically was not independently re-verified from the raw sequence in this session (automated position extraction proved unreliable), so treat the poly-A detail, not the truncation/identity call, as unconfirmed.

cases.citation: Woods-Samuels P, Wong C, Mathias SL, Scott AF, Kazazian HH Jr, Antonarakis SE. 1989. Genomics 4(3):290-296
cases.why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED case (clone JH28L1HS, 2132 bp), a second, independent nondeleterious L1 insertion in the same factor VIII intron reported in the same paper, with an ORF at nt 1-1927. Same caveat as M22333: truncation/identity solid from the primary paper; terminal poly-A specifically not independently re-verified this session.

cases.citation: Sekido R, Takagi T, Okanami M, Moribe H, Yamamura M, Higashi Y, Kondoh H. 1996. Gene 173(2):227-232
cases.why_safe: 5'-TRUNCATED CR1 case. GenBank feature table explicitly annotates a mobile_element of type 'transposon:CR1' at nt 417-952 (536 bp) within an intron of the chicken deltaEF1 gene locus. Full-length CR1 is ~4.5 kb (Haas et al. 1997 J Mol Evol); a 536 bp fragment is therefore heavily 5'-truncated, consistent with Vandergon & Reitman's (1994 Mol Biol Evol 11:886-898) finding that the vast majority of genomic CR1 copies are heavily 5'-truncated. No ORF or poly-A is annotated at this locus; CR1, like other R1-like clade members, is not expected to carry a poly-A tail.

cases.citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); clade established by Kordiš D, Gubenšek F. 1998. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 95(18):10704-10709
cases.why_safe: Dfam-curated family DF000002968 (BovB-1_DR), classified LINE > RTE-group > BovB in zebrafish. BovB is the classic horizontally-transferred RTE-clade LINE (Kordiš & Gubenšek 1998); Dfam family-membership is curated independently of any TEagle-adjacent tool. This is a consensus family model, not a single genomic locus with coordinates, and no poly-A status is assessable at this level -- flagged as lower-resolution evidence than the discrete-locus cases above.

cases.citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); Batzer MA, Deininger PL. 2002. Nat Rev Genet 3(5):370-379
cases.why_safe: Dfam family DF000000002 = AluY, the youngest/most active human Alu subfamily, curated independently of any TEagle output. NON-AUTONOMOUS: Alu elements have no ORFs or reverse transcriptase of their own and are mobilized in trans by L1 ORF2p (Dewannieux et al. 2003 Nat Genet 35:41-48). TEagle is not expected to classify this as an autonomous LINE; correctly declining an autonomous-LINE call here is itself informative.

cases.citation: Storer J, Hubley R, Rosen J, Wheeler TJ, Smit AFA. 2021. Mobile DNA 12:2 (Dfam resource); Krayev AS, Kramerov DA, Skryabin KG, Ryskov AP, Bayev AA, Georgiev GP. 1980. Nucleic Acids Res 8(6):1201-1215
cases.why_safe: Dfam family DF000001733 = B1_Mm, the mouse counterpart of primate Alu (both derived from 7SL RNA, independently amplified). NON-AUTONOMOUS SINE: no ORF1/ORF2 of its own, mobilized in trans by an autonomous LINE partner.

cases.citation: Medhora, Maruyama & Hartl 1991 Genetics 128(2):311-318
cases.why_safe: Identity high (record clone=Mos1, matches the canonical Medhora/Maruyama/Hartl 1991 Mos1 papers) but the GenBank record is PARTIAL at both ends (misc_feature <1..>1293) with NO annotated CDS or TIR coordinates. Do not claim record-level TIR/ORF coordinates - cite the paper's reported 28-bp TIRs instead. Autonomous per literature.

cases.citation: Franz & Savakis 1991 Nucleic Acids Res 19(23):6646
cases.why_safe: TIR coordinates (1-255 inverted / 1521-1775 inverted) and Tc1-like family identity are solid GenBank-annotated features. Do NOT use as an 'autonomous, TIR-encloses-intact-transposase' example: the deposited copy's transposase region includes a /pseudo-annotated segment (gene/CDS 887..1492, note=pseudo) alongside CDS 347..808 - this specific clone is not confirmed fully functional.

cases.citation: Hehl, Nacken, Krause, Saedler & Sommer 1991 Plant Mol Biol 16(2):369-371
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated 12-bp TIRs (repeat_region 1-12 and 3617-3629, both inverted) directly enclose the Tam3-transposase CDS (848-3097, protein_id CAA38906.1). Autonomous, full-length, coordinates explicit.

cases.citation: Streck, MacGaffey & Beckendorf 1986 EMBO J 5(13):3615-3623
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated left/right terminal repeats (1-12 / 2999-3016) enclose ORF1/transposase CDS (316-2250, protein_id CAA28410.1). This is the classic hobo108 element; explicit coordinates.

cases.citation: Warren, Atkinson & O'Brochta 1994 Genet Res 64(2):87-97
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated inverted TIRs (1-17 / 2733-2749) enclose the complete transposase CDS (450-2288). Autonomous, explicit coordinates.

cases.citation: Nacken, Piotrowiak, Saedler & Sommer 1991 Mol Gen Genet 228(1-2):201-208
cases.why_safe: 13-bp inverted TIRs (1-13 / 15152-15164) explicitly enclose both TNP1 (multi-exon CDS) and TNP2 CDS regions of the Tam1 element in the GenBank feature table. Structural homology to maize En/Spm reported in the paper. Autonomous.

cases.citation: Zabala & Vodkin 2008 BMC Plant Biol 8:124
cases.why_safe: 'Putative autonomous' per the paper's own title. GenBank mobile_element feature gives explicit subrange coordinates (4240-24783, ~20.5 kb) for the Tgmt* CACTA element within a larger F3'H-flanking genomic deposit. Paper text (not broken out as separate GenBank sub-features) reports 13-bp CACTA-type TIRs and a 2194-aa TNP1/TNP2-domain transposase spanning most of the element.

cases.citation: Xu, Yan, Maurais, Fu, O'Brien, Mottinger & Dooner 2004 Plant Cell 16(5):1105-1114
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated 185-bp inverted TIRs (1-185 / 3736-3916) enclose the transposase CDS (join 746-2484,2554-2944, protein_id AAF66982.1). Flag as an atypical/distant Mutator relative: paper reports Jittery excises without reinsertion and its transposase (JITA) is closer to MULE-family MURA proteins than to canonical MuDR.

cases.citation: Li, Harris & Dooner 2013 Plant Cell 25(9):3251-3265
cases.why_safe: GenBank record itself annotates the mobile_element as note='autonomous TED element'; a multi-exon transposase CDS ('TEDA', 513 aa, protein_id AGR45850.1) spans the element. Companion locus record KF279654 shows 9-bp flanking TSDs (1505-1513/5474-5482) bracketing the same 3960-bp element in a bronze1 (bz-m175) insertion. TIR base-pair count is described in the paper rather than itemized as a separate GenBank repeat_region feature in either record.

cases.citation: Cary, Goebel, Corsaro, Wang, Rosen & Fraser 1989 Virology 172(1):156-169
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated terminal (1-13/2460-2472) and internal (17-36/2410-2428) inverted repeats enclose the transposase CDS (329-2113, protein_id AAA87375.2). This is the original piggyBac/IFP2 clone, independent of TEagle's excluded M11240 (verified separately to actually be a D. melanogaster copia LTR retrotransposon record, not piggyBac).

cases.citation: Luo, Li, Han, Guo, Yang, Wu, Zhang, Liu, Qian & Fang 2014 BMC Mol Biol 15:28
cases.why_safe: GenBank-annotated outer (1-13/2394-2406) and inner (352-376/2247-2271) inverted repeats enclose the transposase CDS (613-2130, protein_id AGK25052.1). Independent second piggyBac-like case, different organism from IFP2 and from TEagle's own OQ718454 (excluded for other reasons, see supply_assessment).

cases.coords: 996..3902 (mobile_element span within a 4734-bp deposited plasmid record)
cases.citation: O'Hare & Rubin 1983 Cell 34(1):25-35
cases.why_safe: CAVEAT FIRST: the deposited GenBank record's own SOURCE field is 'synthetic construct' - this is a cloned transformation-vector plasmid (pPI25.1), not a genomic insertion. That said, the annotated mobile_element span (996-3902) is exactly 2907 bp, matching the well-documented complete P-element length, flanked by GenBank-annotated 8-bp direct repeats (988-995/3903-3910) consistent with target-site duplication footprint reported by O'Hare & Rubin 1983. Confidence held at medium specifically because of the vector-context caveat.

cases.citation: Black, Jackson, Kidwell & Dover 1987 EMBO J 6(13):4125-4135
cases.why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: internally-deleted P-element derivative (1170 bp vs the 2907-bp complete P element). TIRs preserved and GenBank-annotated (inverted repeat A: 9-39, inverted repeat A': 1132-1162) but NO transposase CDS is annotated - the transposase-encoding region is deleted; the element instead encodes the truncated KP repressor protein. TEagle should not call this autonomous.

cases.citation: Kikuchi, Terauchi, Wada & Hirano 2003 Nature 421(6919):167-170
cases.why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: 430-bp MITE (mPing/miniSNOOPY), GenBank record has NO CDS annotated at all (correctly, since MITEs by definition lack the transposase), mobilized in trans by the autonomous Ping/Mutator-family element per Kikuchi et al 2003.

cases.citation: Moschetti et al. 2008 Mol Genet Genomics 279(5):451-461
cases.why_safe: NON-AUTONOMOUS: GenBank-annotated inverted TIRs (1-17/1249-1265, Bari1-family) are intact, but the internal CDS (135-1131) is explicitly annotated /pseudo (pseudogenized transposase) - TEagle should not call this autonomous.

cases.citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK, Lenz J (2001) Curr Biol 11:1531-1535
cases.why_safe: GenBank complete-genome record (9472 bp) annotates both LTRs (1-968, 8504-9472), a gag-pro-pol ORF (1112-6746, with the two -1 frameshifts typical of HML-2) and a putative env ORF (6451-8550, protein AAL18258.1) encoding envelope; full-length, human-specific insertion described by Turner et al. 2001.

cases.citation: Turner G, Barbulescu M, Su M, Jensen-Seaman MI, Kidd KK, Lenz J (2001) Curr Biol 11:1531-1535
cases.why_safe: Complete-genome record (9463 bp), sister locus to K113 from the same study: both LTRs (1-960, 8496-9463) annotated, gag-pro-pol ORF (1104-6740, two -1 frameshifts) and putative env ORF (6442-8541, protein AAL18259.1).

cases.citation: Ono M, Yasunaga T, Miyata T, Ushikubo H (1986) J Virol 60:589-598
cases.why_safe: The original HERV-K10 sequence: GenBank annotates two gag CDS (1112-1963, 1807-3111), a protease-subunit CDS (3639-3917) and both LTRs (1-968, 8212-9179), so gag and protease presence is solid. The downstream pol/env region is annotated in this record as a single long ORF (4172-8257, ~4.1 kb) rather than two separately bounded genes, so the exact pol/env domain boundary is not independently confirmed from this record alone -- use gag/protease at high confidence, env presence at medium confidence pending boundary check against the published ORF map in Ono et al. 1986.

cases.citation: Hanger JJ, Bromham LD, McKee JJ, O'Brien TM, Robinson WF (2000) J Virol 74:4264-4272
cases.why_safe: Complete koala retrovirus (KoRV) genome (8431 bp): gag (961-2526), pol (2641-6024), env (5906-7885) and both LTRs (1-505, 7927-8431) all annotated by the original describing paper. GenBank organism field records the viral taxon (Koala retrovirus); host species (koala) is unambiguous since KoRV is koala-specific and actively endogenizing.

cases.citation: Wang Y, Liu S, Li J, Han M, Wang Z (2008) Virologica Sinica 23:15-24
cases.why_safe: Complete endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (enJSRV) genome (7942 bp) deposited directly under the host organism Ovis aries: gag (583-2433), pro (2325-3194), pol (3440-5742), env (5682-7517), both LTRs (1-435, 7497-7932) annotated.

cases.citation: Tang HB, Ouyang K, Ma L, Bai A, Qin S, Chen F, Lin J, Cao Y, Wu J (2015) Genome Announc 3:e00620-15
cases.why_safe: Complete porcine endogenous retrovirus C (PERV-C) genome (8774 bp): gag (1081-2655), pol (2803-6240, full-length span consistent with intact PR-RT-RNaseH-IN), env (6116-8080), both LTRs (1-639, 8149-8774) annotated. GenBank organism field is the viral taxon (Porcine endogenous retrovirus C); host (domestic pig) is unambiguous for this virus.

cases.citation: Kato S, Matsuo K, Nishimura N, Takahashi N, Takano T (1987) Jpn J Genet 62:127-137
cases.why_safe: Complete baboon endogenous virus (BaEV) strain M7 proviral genome (8507 bp): gag (985-2598), pol (2575-6165), env (6235-7926), both LTRs (1-555, 7953-8507) annotated. The GenBank organism field itself reads 'Baboon endogenous virus strain M7' rather than a host binomial, and the paper's own title describes this as a chimeric genome (gag/pol resembling murine type-C gammaretroviruses, env resembling type-D betaretroviruses); superfamily left blank because the biology is genuinely a natural recombinant, and the exact Papio host species is not stated in the record I could verify.

cases.citation: Herr W (1984) J Virol 49:471-478
cases.why_safe: Complete AKV murine leukemia virus proviral genome (8374 bp) from AKR mice: gag-pol polyprotein ORF (639-5843) with separately annotated gag polyprotein (639-2252) and protease mat_peptide (2238-2612), env polyprotein (5783-7792, gp70+p15E), both LTRs annotated (1-144 and 7825->8374, with terminal reiterations). gate_verdict:
Three cases found, all from a single GenBank record (AF123535, the Tikhonov et al. 1999 PNAS 160-kb maize adh1-F contig, a direct descendant of the SanMiguel et al. 1996 Science nested-retrotransposon locus). This record is a strong source class because the submitting authors themselves annotated individual retrotransposons as split, multi-segment mobile_element features (GenBank join() locations spanning tens of kb, with nested opposite-strand insertions occupying the gaps) -- i.e. condition (a) is directly visible in the primary deposit's own feature table, not inferred. Superfamily assignment for every family name (Ji, Opie, Victim = Copia; Milt, Cinful, Tekay, Huck, Reina, Grande = Gypsy) is independently tabulated in Meyers, Tingey & Morgante 2001 Genome Res 11:1660-1676 (Table 1), built on the original RT-phylogeny grouping in SanMiguel et al. 1996/1998 -- satisfying condition (b) independent of TEagle.

I could not reach n=5 within this pass, and I do not think this specific class (nested, opposite-strand-interrupted LTR-RT deposits with an independently confirmed superfamily) is abundant enough to casually reach 5 well-verified cases. Two adjacent leads did not pan out on inspection: (1) the orthologous sorghum BAC in the same paper (AF124045) only records "insertion site duplication" markers for Milt/Fourf/Victim, not the retrotransposons themselves as annotated features with coordinates, so it cannot supply a coords-anchored case; (2) the barley Rar1 locus (AF254799, Shirasu et al. 2000 Genome Res 10:908-915) has abundant nested LTR-RTs (Nikita, Sukkula, Sabrina, BAGY-2, BARE-1) but nearly all are solo-LTR deletion derivatives with their internal (gag-pol) regions already removed by LTR-LTR recombination -- the ambiguity there is "no coding region survives at all," not "IN/RT present but unreadable due to strand/overlap," so it does not cleanly fit the panel's mechanism and I excluded it rather than force it. I also note (per the advisor review of my own approach) that a whole element deposited entirely on the minus strand, with no internal rearrangement, does NOT qualify under TEagle's stated gate (reverse-complementing recovers a fully readable IN/RT order); I did not use any such case.

Reaching n=5 for this panel would most likely require systematic mining of Triticeae BAC annotation tables (Wicker et al. and successors, which tabulate per-element strand/coordinates against TREP family) or querying Dfam's genomic-coordinate hit tables for family members landing on the reverse strand relative to a larger annotated span -- neither was completed in this session's search budget. I recommend narrowing the paper's Panel 4.1 claim to reflect an n=3 gate-triggering set (or explicitly flagging it as an open collection effort) rather than padding to 5 with lower-confidence or borderline cases.

26 cases assembled from 4 primary sources (Bowen & McDonald 2001 Drosophila Table 3; Fu, Zheng & Dooner 2002 maize bz1-locus paper AF391808; Turner et al. 2001 and Subramanian et al. 2011 for human HERV-K/HML-2), spanning three kingdoms (insect, plant, human) and three independent evidence chains, so no single paper or family dominates.

Bucket coverage is real but lopsided, and I did not pad it:
- >=98% (young): 14 cases -- well supplied (11 Drosophila elements, all with individual accessions and identities of 98.5-100% from a single peer-reviewed table; plus maize Zeon1 100% and Fourf 98.2% from AF391808; plus human HERV-K113 with an explicitly stated 100%-identical LTR pair).
- 85-97% (intermediate): 10 cases -- five maize elements from the same AF391808 nested cluster (RIRE1 97.1%, Prem1 94.6%, Prem2b 91.6%, Opie2 91.2%, Huck2 85.8%) plus five HERV-K loci (K104, K115, K11, K12, K70) whose identity I derived from Subramanian et al.'s own stated age ranges and substitution-rate formula rather than a printed percentage -- flagged medium confidence accordingly.
- 72-84% (the floor, most wanted): 0 confirmed cases despite the largest share of search effort. This is a genuine gap, not an oversight I chose to leave unfilled. Two structural reasons kept surfacing across sources: (1) most quantitatively-tabulated systems (Drosophila euchromatic elements, human HML-2, most Adh1-region maize insertions) are simply too young for the substitution rates involved to reach 16-28% divergence within the time depths the primary literature reports; (2) intact LTR pairs that do get old enough tend to have already resolved to solo LTRs via unequal recombination (documented half-lives of ~0.5-0.8 My for intact pairs in rice/maize), so the literature's "old" examples jump straight past the floor to either solo-LTR remnants (no pair to compare) or heavily fragmented relics like the one case I did find.
- <72% (clearly degraded): 1 case -- maize Prem2a at 63.8% identity, explicitly stated in Fu, Zheng & Dooner 2002, described by the authors as "highly fragmented," which is exactly the kind of relic that persists at this divergence; I marked it medium confidence for that reason.

I searched extensively (SanMiguel/Bennetzen maize paleontology series, Vitte & Panaud and Piegu rice solo-LTR papers, Ma & Bennetzen, Devos/Brunner wheat and multi-locus maize comparisons, Belshaw and Johnson & Coffin HERV papers, several ancient-ERV Mobile DNA papers) for additional 72-84% examples and could not find a case where a paper both (a) states or clearly derives a specific LTR-LTR identity in that exact band and (b) ties it to a verifiable accession or coordinate-anchored region -- most of those sources report only family-level or genome-wide aggregate divergence statistics (means, ranges, half-lives) rather than per-element numbers I could safely attribute to a named, citable locus. Rather than force a fit by mislabeling a borderline case (e.g., pushing Huck2's 85.8% down into the floor bucket, which I did not do) or estimating an accession I could not verify, I am reporting the shortfall directly. If TEagle's own benchmark protocol can tolerate examples where the identity is derived-from-age via a paper's own stated clock (as I did for the HERV-K intermediate cases), that same approach applied to a slower-clock, older-diverging animal ERV lineage (e.g., older non-HML-2 human ERV families, or bovine/murine ERVs with faster substitution rates) is the most promising next avenue, but I did not have verified per-locus data for those in hand and chose not to include them speculatively.

I verified 12 negative-control cases via direct primary-source lookup (NCBI efetch/Gene records plus the cited literature), spanning all 5 requested categories, but this falls well short of the requested "at least 25, balanced." Category breakdown: single-copy protein-coding genes = 4 (C. elegans, Arabidopsis, S. cerevisiae, human), satellite/tandem repeat = 1, low-complexity/simple-sequence = 1, RT-like/DNase-like/tyrosine-recombinase host genes = 5 (this category came out strongest, consistent with the task's own note that it is the most informative), rRNA/tRNA arrays = 1.

Categories 2 (satellite), 3 (low-complexity) and 5 (rRNA/tRNA) are under-supplied. This is a verification-throughput limit, not a supply limit in principle: for every accession I tried to recall/guess and then confirm (mouse major satellite X14345/X60984, Arabidopsis pAL1 centromeric repeat M65137, Huntingtin CAG repeat L27350, Kreitman's Drosophila Adh alleles K02071/M19547/M17836, an original APEX1 cDNA clone number, an E. coli rrnB tRNA-array accession, an NCBI Gene enumeration for yeast tRNA clusters), the confirmation step failed to return a verifiable match, so per the hard rule against inventing accessions I dropped every one of them rather than report an unverified identifier. I also deliberately dropped two candidates whose primary literature undercuts their "negative" status: Cre recombinase (X03453, phage-encoded, not a host gene) and the maize 180-bp knob repeat (the primary paper explicitly asks "are chromosome knobs megatransposons?", i.e., the label itself is contested).

Bulk enumeration via NCBI esearch (rather than recall-then-confirm) is the correct route to close categories 2/3/5 to the requested count, but the web-fetch summarization tool I have access to proved unreliable at parsing esearch XML output within the session's remaining budget (it conflated nuccore and gene/PubMed result sets on two occasions), so I stopped rather than risk transcribing a wrong ID as verified. A follow-up pass with programmatic (non-summarized) XML parsing of esearch/efetch results, applied to titles like "satellite DNA[Title]", "microsatellite[Title]", "tRNA gene cluster[Title]" restricted by organism, should be able to reach the target count with the same verification standard used here.

20 Copia (Ty1) and 21 Gypsy (Ty3) cases delivered, meeting the >=20/panel target, all independently verified against live NCBI GenBank records (accession, organism, length/feature-table coordinates) via NCBI E-utilities, with primary-literature or GenBank-annotation-based superfamily calls established independently of any TEagle output. None overlap the five excluded development accessions (M11240, M12927, M80343, X01005, X05424).

Coverage and honest limits:
- Taxonomic spread achieved: insects (Drosophila melanogaster x6 Copia+Gypsy combined, D. buzzatii, Bombyx mori, Anopheles gambiae), fungi (Saccharomyces cerevisiae x2, Magnaporthe grisea x2, Cladosporium fulvum, Fusarium oxysporum), plants (Zea mays x7 across both panels, Hordeum vulgare, Nicotiana tabacum, Solanum tuberosum, Triticum aestivum/turgidum, Arabidopsis thaliana, Glycine max, Vitis vinifera, Quercus suber, Pinus radiata, Pinus pinaster), nematode (Caenorhabditis elegans), and vertebrates (Gadus morhua for Gypsy; Pyxicephalus adspersus for Copia).
- Genuine skew, not an oversight: Zea mays is the best-annotated genome for both superfamilies in the classic literature (SanMiguel/Bennetzen adh1-region lineage of papers), so it appears 7 times across the two panels; Drosophila melanogaster appears 6 times because it is the historical source of both the Copia and Gypsy type elements and most of the named gypsy-clade families (297, ZAM, Idefix, Tirant, 1731, mdg1). Vertebrate Copia (Ty1) is represented by only one case (Pyxicephalus adspersus, Tpa1, X74338), and that case is a ~225 bp degenerate-PCR RT-domain fragment, not a full-length element -- this reflects a real scarcity of full-length, discretely deposited Ty1/copia elements from vertebrates in GenBank, not incomplete searching.
- Some entries carry documented structural caveats (noted in why_safe): MAGGY, Idefix and Ty4 records are partial for one gene; Tirant's record is shorter than the literature-reported full-length consensus; Cinful-1 is a naturally gag-deficient element; Gmr1 has an atypical (copia-like) pol domain order despite being phylogenetically Gypsy and should be treated as a deliberate edge case, not a canonical exemplar, if used in domain-order-sensitive tests.
- Elements investigated but deliberately omitted because no single, unambiguous, discrete GenBank accession could be confirmed within the hard rule against inventing accessions: Tos17 (rice), element "412" (Drosophila), Ty2 and Ty5 (S. cerevisiae), Tvv1 and Diaspora (soybean/grapevine, fragmentary GenBank deposits only), Reme1 (melon, only short mRNA-clone fragments on GenBank), RIRE1 (rice), Boty (Botrytis cinerea), full-length Micropia (Drosophila), and a standalone Grande-1 record (only available bundled inside large multi-element BAC/contig sequences without independently confirmed sub-coordinates for that specific family).
- Search budget note: the session's WebSearch quota (200 calls) was exhausted during this compilation; the last several verifications and citation checks were completed via NCBI E-utilities (esearch/esummary/efetch) directly against GenBank flat files, which is the more authoritative source for accession-to-citation linkage in any case.
- Two entries (Fatima in GU817319, and the Ji/Opie/Huck maize copies in AF123535) are coordinate-based genomic-region citations rather than discrete single-element accessions, as explicitly preferred by the task instructions for panel 5.2 boundary comparison.

Coverage achieved: 8 full-length/near-full-length autonomous LINEs spanning 6 clades (L1 x2 species, I, Jockey, R2, R1, R4, RTE); 4 clearly-marked 5'-truncated LINEs (Jockey, two independent human L1-in-F8-intron insertions, one chicken CR1 fragment) covering 3 different clades in the truncated state; both poly-A-tailed (L1RP, L1spa, Jockey -- each confirmed against an explicit statement in the primary literature, not raw sequence inspection) and non-poly-A-tailed 3' structures (I factor's tandem TAA repeats, R2's structured 3' UTR, R1's AT-rich terminus); and 2 non-autonomous SINEs (AluY, B1_Mm), both explicitly labeled non-autonomous.

What I attempted and could not confirm to the accession-level bar, so omitted rather than guessed: the original Kazazian et al. 1988 Nature hemophilia-A L1 insertions (no accession locatable; I substituted the related but distinct Woods-Samuels et al. 1989 Genomics polymorphic F8-intron L1 insertions, which are equally well-documented 5'-truncated cases); the Miki et al. 1992 Cancer Res APC-gene L1 insertion (no accession found); Kimberland et al. 1999's second element, L1beta-thal (no accession found); a discrete full-length (non-truncated) single-locus CR1 sequence (only a truncated genomic instance and a Dfam consensus family were confirmed -- no full-length CR1 locus with coordinates was located in the time available); trypanosome SLACS/CRE-clade elements (only two small, unpublished subclone fragments, 373 and 550 bp, were found -- too fragmentary and provenance-uncertain to trust); and a tRNA-derived SINE distinct from the 7SL-derived Alu/B1 pair (e.g., rodent ID element -- no accession confirmed). The BovB/RTE and CR1-family cases rest on Dfam library membership rather than a discrete locus, which is weaker evidence than the GenBank-record cases and is flagged as medium confidence accordingly. A tool-reliability issue is worth noting for reuse: the WebFetch summarizer cannot reliably index exact base positions within large GenBank flat files (it fabricated inconsistent poly-A readouts for the same record across repeated queries), so every poly-A claim in this panel is anchored to an explicit textual statement in the primary literature or a GenBank FEATURES annotation rather than to raw sequence extraction.

Reason for the shortfall: every candidate accession recalled from training or surfaced by WebSearch had to be independently re-verified against live NCBI records via esearch/esummary/efetch, because WebSearch repeatedly returned wrong or nonexistent accessions with confident-sounding justification (e.g. it asserted X55322=Tam3 when the record is actually human NCAM mRNA; AB011403=Tol2 when it is a plant virus segment; U62371=Himar1 when it is an SIV gene; X53585=Minos when it is rat Hsp60; and it 're-confirmed' X06779 as the P element via search-summary text even after a direct efetch had already shown its SOURCE field is 'synthetic construct'). Each surviving case therefore cost several verification round-trips, which capped the achievable count for this session. 20 cases assembled, all accessions confirmed to exist and match the stated description via direct NCBI E-utilities record retrieval (efetch/esearch/esummary against nuccore/pubmed), not from memory. WebSearch was exhausted after the first call in this session, so all verification ran through NCBI's E-utilities rather than general web/journal search -- this narrowed coverage toward well-indexed GenBank complete-genome depositions and away from cases that would need a journal's own site or a review article to locate. Coverage: 12 full-length proviruses with both LTRs and env (human HERV-K x3 incl. one with a domain-boundary caveat, koala, sheep, pig, baboon-chimeric, mouse AKV-MLV, mouse MMTV, cat RD-114 x2, simian type-D with unresolved host species); 2 env-less proviruses (mouse IAP, mouse MusD -- both are the classical Class-II-like mouse ERV families, and this was the thinnest category: I found no comparably well-documented non-rodent env-deletion locus with a genuine primary-literature domain description in the time available); 4 solo LTRs across two independent papers/families (human HML-2 at RASGRF2, chimp+bonobo HERV-K3p25 orthologs, gorilla HERV-H) -- the fourth candidate I initially found (feline RD-114 clone 'EX-LTR') was dropped because the record only supports 'isolated LTR clone,' not a confirmed solo-LTR (post-recombination) locus, and a wrong solo-LTR label would corrupt exactly the hard-negative case this panel needs; 2 intermediate cases (human and chimp ERVWE1/syncytin loci, where env is intact/functional but gag-pol is an explicitly documented pseudogene) that add domain-asymmetry diversity beyond the simple full/lacking-env split. Non-human organisms represented: koala, sheep, pig, baboon, mouse (x4 distinct loci), cat (x3), Old-World-monkey/simian, chimpanzee (x3), bonobo, gorilla -- well beyond 'a few.' Two accessions carry an explicit confidence caveat rather than being silently smoothed over: M14123 (HERV-K10) because the GenBank record collapses pol and env into one long downstream ORF without a resolved internal boundary, so env-domain precision at that locus is medium confidence; U85505 (simian endogenous retrovirus) because the specific Old-World-monkey host species could not be confirmed from the record metadata retrieved, so only the class/superfamily/domain-content claims are made at confidence, not a host binomial. One candidate case (DQ112150, chimpanzee CERV-K10) was found and then explicitly excluded because its GenBank record carries no CDS annotation at all, so no domain content could be attributed to it from the source I checked.

Delivered 2 of the target 20 primer-pair cases and 3 of the target 15 copy-number cases, both far short of target. This reflects tool constraints encountered this session, not literature scarcity -- published TE-specific primer pairs and assembly-anchored copy-number statements are common in the literature; I could not reach most of them with the tools available.

Root causes, by panel:
- Panel A (primers): WebSearch was exhausted (200/200) before I could use it at all, so all discovery relied on Europe PMC's REST search via WebFetch. The dominant failure mode was that essentially every post-2010 paper I checked (10+ candidates: PIF/Pong/Harbinger in maize, Ac/Ds and Mu1 flanking genotyping, MHC-region Alu insertions, AluYb8/9 diagnostic loci, mPing/BonnMu genotyping, ZmSWEET4c hAT insertion) states primers only in a supplementary Excel/PDF table that WebFetch cannot parse. Two cases succeeded because the primers happened to be given inline in the main text/methods (short technical assays with only 2-3 primers). I deliberately declined to reconstruct any primer sequence from training-data memory (e.g., IRAP/REMAP BARE-1 primers, classic Alu insertion-polymorphism primers like PV92/ACE/TPA25) because I could not re-verify the exact 18-25mer sequences character-for-character against a fetched source, and a wrong base in a primer sequence is a worse failure mode than an omitted case. Given unrestricted WebSearch and time, I estimate at least 15-20 more verbatim-verifiable primer pairs are reachable (IS6110 INS1/INS2 for M. tuberculosis, classic Alu insertion polymorphism panels, hAT/CACTA/MULE TE-display primers, additional IRAP/REMAP retrotransposon primers) but they require either a search engine or access to supplementary files, neither fully available here.
- Panel B (copy number): more tractable since counts often appear in abstracts/results (in-body text), but many candidate statements I found were genome-wide proportions (e.g., '20% of the D. melanogaster genome is TE-derived') or subspecies-level ranges rather than an integer count tied to one named assembly, and I dropped those per the panel's own discriminating criterion. I have moderate confidence several more clean cases exist and are reachable with more full-text fetches (e.g., per-family Drosophila release 6 counts, Arabidopsis Col-0 TAIR10 family counts, L1Hs full-length human counts by build) but ran out of session time/tool budget before locating verbatim-quotable statements for them.
